Hah! However you define the rules, kids are going to find a way to bend them to establish a social hierarchy. I wore uniforms from K-12. In middle school, how cool you were was determined by the length of your skirt (within the no more than 3" above the knee guidelines), the height of your socks (they then instituted uniform socks), and whether you wore a cool tshirt under your uniform polo. When they made the rules stricter, the social hierarchy didn't change, but the ways kids expressed it got more bizarre. Bleach stains on your uniform socks became the height of cool and a girl with a skit 4" above her knee was an automatic slut, while a girl with a skirt just below the knee was a prude.

Uniforms are nice in the sense that you don't have to think about which outfit to wear to school, so they save time, but they don't really have the equalizing effect that everyone hopes for.
